title: Parsing a single in-range entry
statement: Fix $w \ge 1$, and let $(\mathrm{idx}, \mathrm{dir})$ be a single entry whose index satisfies $\mathrm{idx} < w$. Then parsing the one-element list $[(\mathrm{idx}, \mathrm{dir})]$ yields the singleton list $[(\mathrm{idx}, \mathrm{dir}, \mathrm{false})]$, where the index is viewed as an element of $\{0, 1, \dots, w-1\}$ and the marker flag is $\mathrm{false}$ (there is no following entry to carry a termination marker).
hypotheses_covered: the entry's index satisfies idx < w
the input list consists of the single entry (idx, dir)
replaced:
Equational lemma: a single in-range entry $(idx, dir)$ parses to the singleton
$[(\langle idx, h\rangle, dir, \mathrm{false})]$.
